To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the metabolic activation of dimethyl nitrosamine (DMNA) to cytotoxic and mutagenic intermediates is a linear function of the amount of enzyme present, and that the degree and nature of DMNA induced damage in vitro are independent of the activity of the cytochrome P 450 dependent monooxygenases in the S 9 fraction.
the metabolic activation of DMN to cytotoxic and mutagenic products in vitro by rat liver post mitochondrial supernatant is a function of the concentration of S15 fraction in the assay mixture.

the degree of cytotoxic and mutagenic effects induced by DMN in V79 cells in vitro are linearly related and are not related to the activity of the 3-methylcholanthrene or phenobarbital induced mixed function oxidase systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolic activation of dimethyl nitrosamine to mutagenic intermediates in vitro.
the in vitro metabolic transformation of DMN to mutagenic intermediates and the relationship between the activity of the enzymes involved in this process and the degree of mutagenicity induced.
the development and application of a quantitative mammalian cell assay for chemical mutagens/carcinogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the degree of mutagenicity and cytotoxicity induced by DMN in vitro is dependent on the concentration of S15 fraction in the incubation mixture and that the degree is not dependent on the EROD and EMND activities in the S 1 5 fraction.
the metabolic activation of DMN to mutagenic intermediates in vitro is dependent on the concentration of S15 fraction in the assay mixture, but is not related to EROD activity or EMND activity.

DMN is activated to mutagenic or cytotoxic intermediates by a mechanism which does not involve either phenobarbital or 3 methylchloanthrene inducibility and is not related to the activity of EROD or EMND.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metabolic activation of DMN to cytotoxic and mutagenic products in vitro by the S 15 preparation from rat liver is a nonenzymatic process.
the metabolic activation of DMN by the S 15 fractions of rat liver to cytotoxic and/or mutagenic metabolites is not dependent upon EROD or EMND activities.

the degree of mutagenicity induced by DMN in vitro is linearly related to the degree of cytotoxic damage induced by DMN, and that the cytotoxic damage induced in V79 Chinese hamsters cells by DMN is dependent on the enzyme content of the rat S 15 fraction and not on the enzyme inducer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DMN is metabolically activated to cytotoxic and mutagenic intermediates in a manner which is independent of the EROD and EMND activity of the S 1S fraction.
the S 15 enzyme system is capable of producing mutagenic and cytotoxic intermediates from DMN.

the degree of mutagenicity and cytotoxicity induced by DMN in V79 cells is directly proportional to the amount of S 15 enzyme preparation used to metabolize DMN and is independent of the activity of EROD and EMND.
